dims.name: Product / technology
dims.why: Karthik Agro runs one grain plant with ENA, fuel ethanol, DDGS, food-grade CO₂, 8.4 MW captive power and zero liquid discharge, a complete grain-distillery set-up. TruAlt adds dual-feed (65% of capacity) and CBG units; AABL and Globus carry ENA through to their own liquor brands.

dims.name: Customers and concentration
dims.why: The subject sells ENA to beverage, pharma and personal-care buyers as well as fuel ethanol to OMCs; the deal file does not give the split. TruAlt and Gulshan depend mainly on OMC ethanol (Gulshan ethanol ₹1,609 Cr of ₹2,314 Cr), while AABL and Globus also sell their own brands to consumers.

dims.name: Entry barriers
dims.why: Distillery licences, environmental clearance and ZLD compliance protect all six. AABL and Globus add state excise brand registrations and liquor distribution, which a pure ENA/ethanol plant such as the subject does not have.

dims.name: Distribution / reach
dims.why: The subject is a single-site B2B seller in Karnataka. Globus sells branded liquor across several states; AABL is entering Odisha, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh; Gulshan runs plants in UP, MP and Assam.

dims.name: Scale of operations
dims.why: At 245 KLPD and ₹862 Cr revenue, the subject is about one-eighth of TruAlt's 2,000 KLPD and under a third of Gulshan's 810 KLPD. Its revenue is close to AABL's ₹1,020 Cr.

dims.name: Management and governance
dims.why: The subject's account was an NPA in 2014-15 and was resolved through an ARC (repaid FY21), and it has no listed disclosure record. AABL, Globus and Gulshan have long listed histories. TruAlt listed in Sep 2025 and is litigating allocation shortfalls. CIAN grew mainly by acquisition.

dims.name: Growth runway
dims.why: The subject is expanding from 245 to 450 KLPD, and the memorandum projects PAT rising from ₹13.0 Cr to ₹45.9 Cr in FY27E; the 450 KLPD status is still unconfirmed. TruAlt has CBG and a proposed SAF project. Globus has no near-term capacity additions, and Gulshan's ₹500 Cr project is awaiting board approval.

dims.name: Feedstock security
dims.why: The deal file describes grain as seasonal, which keeps working capital heavy (₹195.6 Cr of loans against ₹90.8 Cr net worth), and gives no FCI-rice or contract coverage. Gulshan sources about 40% of feedstock as fixed-price FCI rice; TruAlt can switch between cane derivatives and grain.

dims.name: OMC ethanol allocation / offtake
dims.why: The subject runs at full capacity, but the deal file does not give its ESY 2025-26 OMC allocation. Gulshan has an 18 crore-litre ESY 2025-26 allocation and long-term offtake to 2032. TruAlt called its allocation lower than anticipated at 60.6% utilisation, and AABL sold surplus ethanol to private OMCs below breakeven in Q1 FY27. CIAN does not disclose its allocation.

cells: ENA and fuel ethanol, plus DDGS and food-grade CO₂
Merchant ENA, fuel ethanol, own IMIL/IMFL brands
Fuel ethanol; CBG units being built
Diversified: agro, edible oil, sugar, distillery, LPG, healthcare
Grain ethanol, grain processing, mineral chemicals
matrix.why: The subject is a pure distillery with no consumer brand or second business to offset weak ethanol pricing. AABL and Globus earn consumer-liquor margins on part of their ENA.

cells: Five units in Karnataka (Mudhol, Jamkhandi, Badami etc.)
Rajasthan, Haryana, West Bengal, Jharkhand, Bihar
matrix.why: Everything is at one site, so any plant outage or state policy change hits the whole business. TruAlt also runs a 200 KLPD unit in Badami, which puts the two in competition for local grain.

cells: 130 KLPD ethanol + ≈45 mn L/yr ENA (2024 disclosures)
765 KLPD at FY23; +120 KLPD added Apr 2024
matrix.why: The subject is larger than AABL's ethanol unit but far smaller than TruAlt, Gulshan or Globus. If the 450 KLPD expansion is complete, it would approach the mid-sized peers.

≈18 cr L order vs ≈26 cr L capacity, ESY 25-26
matrix.why: Full utilisation puts the subject ahead of TruAlt's 60.6% and Gulshan's allocation-limited ethanol output in the ESY 2025-26 oversupply.

Maize and FCI rice; grain ≈₹21,000/t in Q1 FY27

matrix.why: Peers disclose FCI-rice access or dual-feed flexibility. The deal file does not show what protects the subject from grain price swings.

18 cr L ESY 25-26; LTOA ≈13 cr L/yr to 2032
matrix.why: Allocation is the main revenue swing factor for ESY 2025-26, and the subject's figure needs to come from diligence. Gulshan's long-term offtake is the strongest disclosed in this set.

cells: DDGS, food-grade CO₂; 8.4 MW captive power; ZLD
CBG plants (10–20 TPD each) under build
matrix.why: The subject's CO₂ sales and captive power are standard for a modern grain plant and are matched by most peers.
The subject has the lowest margins in the set. The 10x FY27E pricing assumes PAT margin rising to 4.5%.
The subject carries the highest leverage in the set; part of the ₹35 Cr round goes to working capital and capex.
Peers have daily price discovery and liquidity. Subject shares are illiquid until listing and then locked in for six months.

barriers.name: Distillery licences and environmental clearance
barriers.note: New grain distilleries need state excise licences, environmental clearance and pollution-board consent. The subject's Badami plant has operated since 2007 and runs zero liquid discharge.

barriers.name: Capital intensity and scale
barriers.note: At 245 KLPD the subject is well below TruAlt (2,000 KLPD) and Gulshan (≈810 KLPD), and a new 200+ KLPD grain plant can be built within about two years. TruAlt already runs 200 KLPD in Badami.

barriers.name: Feedstock access and working capital
barriers.note: Grain is bought seasonally and financed with debt (₹195.6 Cr loans vs ₹90.8 Cr net worth). Peers with FCI rice or dual-feed capacity have more flexibility.

barriers.name: OMC ethanol allocation
barriers.note: Ethanol volumes and prices are set through OMC tenders and government policy. ESY 2025-26 had industry oversupply and allocation litigation reaching the Supreme Court, so a supply contract gives the subject little protection.

barriers.name: ENA customer relationships
barriers.note: ENA sales to beverage, pharma and personal-care buyers rely on quality approvals and repeat supply. This gives the subject some diversification beyond OMCs, but it has no consumer brand.

barriers.name: Integrated by-products and captive power
barriers.note: DDGS, food-grade CO₂ and 8.4 MW captive power lower net cost per litre. Most scaled grain peers have similar set-ups.

ahead: Running at 100% of 245 KLPD while TruAlt reports 60.6% utilisation and Gulshan's ESY 2025-26 allocation (18 cr L) covers about 69% of its ≈26 cr L ethanol capacity.
Revenue grew 20.7% in FY26 (₹714 Cr to ₹862 Cr), ahead of every peer except CIAN (+116%, acquisition-led); AABL fell 5.1% and TruAlt 9.4%.
ROE of 14.3% on March 2026 net worth is near the top of the set (Gulshan 14.9%, AABL 12.7%), against 6.4% for TruAlt.
Sells ENA to beverage, pharma and personal-care buyers as well as fuel ethanol, and has zero liquid discharge and 8.4 MW captive power at the plant.
behind: Smallest margins in the set: FY26 EBITDA margin 7.4% and PAT margin 1.5%, against a peer median of 14.0% and 5.6%.
Highest leverage: debt/equity 2.2x (₹195.6 Cr loans on ₹90.8 Cr net worth) against a peer range of 0.1x–1.1x.
Scale: 245 KLPD is about one-eighth of TruAlt's 2,000 KLPD, and TruAlt also runs a 200 KLPD unit in Badami competing for local grain.
Credit history includes an NPA in 2014-15 resolved through an ARC (repaid FY21); peers have long listed disclosure records.
watch: Confirmation of the 450 KLPD expansion (memorandum says done, teaser says planned) and its commissioning date.
ESY 2026-27 OMC allocation and tender prices: peers report ethanol realisations of ₹51–64/litre against breakeven of ₹57–60/litre.
H1 FY27 results tracking toward the ₹45.9 Cr FY27E PAT and the 10.6% EBITDA margin the projection implies.
Debt reduction from the round and IPO proceeds, and the outcome of the Supreme Court allocation litigation, which covers the whole industry.
valuation: P/E on audited FY26 PAT at the round's pre-money is 35.3x against a peer median of 12.3x; EV/EBITDA is 10.3x against a peer median of 8.0x. The round is priced at 10x FY27E PAT, which depends on PAT rising 3.5x.
